data.description:
## Context / Problem
`BindingStore` is the authoritative local-id ↔ Jira identity aggregate and must remain so, but its 799-line module now owns byte persistence, live/reverse lifecycle policy, retirement, recovery, peer-state delegates, comment identity, and GET rotation. New safety rules have no cohesive owner, and production code mutates an inner entry returned by the shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility query. A mechanical split could regress hard-won crash, index-lag, identity, serialization, and selective-publication behavior.

## Outcome
Keep one public `BindingStore` facade and existing import/method compatibility while extracting three internal owners: a byte-preserving repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, and incomplete-operation recovery. Typed views remain open over the original dictionaries so unknown fields and exact JSON behavior survive. Add the approved journal-free retirement completion rule: a durable tombstone is intent, and a live forward/reverse pair is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree.

## Delivery slices
1. Extract repository/unit-of-work persistence behind the facade with byte, fault-cut, corruption, rotation-order, and selective-publication regression oracles.
2. Extract lifecycle policy and add narrow facade operations so new production code no longer needs mutation-through-query while `all_bindings()` remains shallow-compatible.
3. Extract recovery, cut the live caller to the narrow mutation seam, and complete exact-match interrupted retirements only at a validated write-bearing operation boundary.

## Architectural constraints
- Preserve `peer_state.py`, `get_rotation.py`, pending → confirmed → reversible retired lifecycle, numeric-ID re-key, comment identity, and the existing five-file selective tickets publication.
- Preserve unknown fields, `indent=2`, sorted keys, trailing newline, legacy additive reads, and unchanged-pass byte/HEAD idempotency.
- Corrupt live state still fails closed; retired/rotation/alert/commit failure behavior changes only when this plan names it.
- Construction, load, check, dry-run, preview, and filtered operations do not perform recovery writes.
- No general journal, format migration, eager rewrite, broad `git add -A`, deep-copy change to `all_bindings()`, or new identity writer.

## Compatibility / rollback
Each slice is an internal facade delegation with unchanged stored formats and public signatures. A slice can be reverted independently to the preceding facade implementation. The exact-match repair is additive and idempotent: disabling its live-operation call restores the prior detectable overlap without rewriting coherent stores.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Existing `BindingStore` imports, signatures, shallow `all_bindings()` behavior, unknown-field preservation, and exact serialization remain compatible through direct-loader and public-facade tests.
- [ ] Repository fault-cut tests preserve current rotation-before-live ordering, per-file atomic replacement, selective five-file publication, and explicit failure outcomes.
- [ ] Lifecycle tests preserve both-index identity guards, pending/confirmed/retired rules, 404 grace/reset, immutable-ID re-key, tombstone suppression/unretire, and append-only comment identity.
- [ ] Recovery tests prove keyed and keyless create recovery plus exact-match retirement completion are idempotent; identity ambiguity or replace failure safety-aborts without guessing.
- [ ] Load/check/dry-run/preview/filtered tests prove zero recovery writes; only a validated write-bearing operation may repair an interrupted retirement.
- [ ] The architecture record identifies preserved behavior, intentional behavior changes, rollback, and the prohibition on broad tickets-branch staging.
data.title: RP-02 — Decompose binding persistence, lifecycle, and recovery behind BindingStore
